ud4.9:1.2: at one time the Fortunate One was dwelling near Rājagaha, in Bamboo Wood, at the Squirrels’ Feeding Place.
ud4.9:1.3: Then when venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta had gone into hiding, into seclusion, this reflection arose in his mind:
ud4.9:1.4: “There are certainly gains for me, it is certainly a good gain for me,
ud4.9:1.5: that my teacher is the Fortunate One, the Worthy One, the Perfect Sambuddha,
ud4.9:1.6: and that I have gone forth from the home to homelessness in such a well explained Dhamma and Discipline,
ud4.9:1.7: and that my companions in the spiritual life are virtuous, of good character,
ud4.9:1.8: and that I have fulfilled the virtuous (precepts), and that I am composed, and that my mind is one pointed,
ud4.9:1.10: and that I am a Worthy One, pollutant-free, and that I am of great power, of great majesty.
ud4.9:1.12: My life has been fortunate, and my death (will be) fortunate.”
ud4.9:2.1: Then the Fortunate One, knowing with his mind the reflection in venerable Upasena Vaṅgantaputta’s mind, on that occasion uttered this exalted utterance:
ud4.9:3.2: ~ who does not grieve at the end in death,
ud4.9:3.3: If that firm one is one who has seen the state (of peace),
ud4.9:3.4: ~ in the midst of grief he does not grieve.
ud4.9:4.1: For the monk who has cut off the craving for continuity,
ud4.9:4.3: Having totally destroyed the round of births,
ud4.9:4.4: ~ for him there is no continuation in existence.”
